IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_ray_1: Every evening Ray went through his notebook of frequencies, hoping to reach his daughter Annie in Louisville.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_ray_2: When his garden finally came in, Ray talked about planting extra for when Annie came home.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_ray_3: One night Ray heard a faint woman's voice that might have come from Louisville. He asked us for batteries to keep listening.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_ray_4a: Thanks to what we brought, Ray caught the voice again. It was Annie, alive in a church shelter in Louisville.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_ray_4t: Because we sided with Ray at the overturned truck, its food fed his neighbors for a week, and they promised to watch the farm while he went to Louisville.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_ray_4b: The batteries never reached him and the voice was lost. Ray blamed himself and started drinking at night.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_ray_5: Ray fixed up his old pickup to go get Annie, but the battery was dead. He asked us for a car battery.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_ray_5b: Ray wanted one more try at reaching Louisville, but his radio needed parts to reach that far.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_ray_6a: The battery we found started the pickup. Ray set off for Louisville to find Annie, radioing in from the road.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_ray_6b: The pickup never started. Ray stayed on the farm, tending the garden for a daughter he might never see.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_ray_end_bad: There was no way left to reach Louisville. Ray talked less and sometimes left his radio off for days.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_casey_1: Casey's father had been coughing for days, with a fever every night. Between broadcasts she read medical books.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_casey_2: As her father's fever kept climbing, Casey asked us for medicine and water.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_casey_3a: The medicine we sent brought the fever down a little. Braver now, Casey started building a bigger antenna on the roof.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_casey_3b: No medicine came and her father got worse. Casey barely slept and kept the radio on just to hear another voice.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_casey_4s: Because we helped Casey when the strange signal came, her boosted rig reached survivors in Brandenburg. She talked to them every night.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_casey_4x: While we helped someone else, the strange signal went silent. Casey tried not to show how hurt she was.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_casey_4: Her father's cough turned into a chest infection. Casey said she needed real medicine now: antibiotics.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_casey_4b: Her father was fighting for breath. Terrified, Casey begged anyone who would listen for medicine.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_casey_5a: The antibiotics we found saved her father. Casey taught him Morse code at his bedside.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_casey_5b: The medicine came too late and Casey's father died. She kept broadcasting so nobody else would feel alone.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_doc_1: June's clinic had four patients, including a boy with a broken leg who asked every morning when he could walk.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_doc_2: To set the boy's leg properly June needed splints and bandages, and she asked us.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_doc_3a: With the splints we brought, the leg was set. The boy walked on a crutch, and June laughed for the first time in weeks.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_doc_3b: No splints came and the leg healed crooked. The boy would limp for life, and June was bitter about how little she had.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_doc_4f: When the fever swept through, we helped June, and nobody in her clinic died. She would not stop saying so.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_doc_4x: When the fever came we sent the medicine elsewhere, and one of June's patients died. She went cold and quiet.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_doc_4: A stranger stumbled into the clinic with a deep gash, and June had nothing left to close it. She asked us for help.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_doc_5a: With the suture kit we found, the stranger lived. The clinic found its feet; June trained recovered patients as helpers and began to sleep a little.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_doc_5b: The stranger died. June talked about closing the clinic, and she sounded exhausted.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_pike_1: Twelve refugees slept in Brother Pike's church. When a quarrel broke out over rations, he stepped between two men.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_pike_2: The church pantry was nearly empty, and Pike asked us for food for the children.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_pike_3a: The food we sent filled the church. A garden started behind it, and people sang while they worked.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_pike_3b: No food came, and two hungry families left for the city. Pike prayed for them every night.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_pike_4r: When Vic's crew planned to hit the church, we kept it safe, and they never got in. Pike's people called us friends.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_pike_4x: When the raid came we sided with Vic, and the storeroom was emptied. Pike forgave them, but his people were frightened.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_pike_4: After a night of the dead pressing on the church doors, Pike asked us for nails and a hammer to board the windows.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_pike_5a: With the nails and hammer we sent, the windows were boarded. The church became a true refuge, and its Sunday bell drew people from miles around.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_pike_5b: The windows stayed open, and one night the dead broke in. Three people died. Pike blamed himself and moved everyone to the basement.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey_1: Dewey was building a truck she called the Ark out of three wrecks, big enough to carry a dozen people out of the county.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey_2: The Ark's engine needed parts Dewey could not find, so she asked us.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey_3a: With the parts we found, the Ark's engine turned over for the first time. Dewey whooped so loud the dead came to the fence.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey_3b: No parts came and the engine seized. Dewey swore about it constantly; it set her back weeks.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey_4s: When the strange signal came we backed Dewey, and the relay tower's wire gave the Ark lights and a radio. It looked like a real rescue truck.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey_4: Before the Ark could leave the garage, it needed a battery and armor plating.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey_5a: With the battery and plating we found, the Ark ran. Dewey gave rides and dreamed out loud of a convoy out of the county.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey_5b: The Ark was shelved. Dewey fixed other people's cars instead, grumbling, but she still talked about it.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard_1: Sergeant Whitaker's squad was down to seven. Command had been silent for weeks, but he kept the watch schedule anyway.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard_2: Two privates were overheard talking about deserting. Whitaker put them on double watch and said nothing more.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard_3: A fever spread through the camp and the aid kit was empty. Whitaker asked us for antibiotics.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard_4a: The antibiotics we sent beat the fever. The squad was loyal again, and Whitaker grudgingly admitted civilians had come through.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard_4b: No medicine came. One soldier died of the fever and two deserted in the night. Whitaker was stone-faced.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard_4t: We sided with Whitaker at the overturned truck, and its military cargo restocked the camp. He began planning to clear the highway checkpoint.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard_5: Whitaker asked us for ammunition and dressings for the operation to clear the highway checkpoint.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard_6a: With the ammunition we sent, the squad cleared the checkpoint. Whitaker let civilians through safely and sounded almost proud.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard_6b: The operation failed and the squad fell back to camp. Whitaker was more closed off than ever.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats_1: Vic's crew was six people. His second, Dutch, kept pushing to rob survivors instead of scavenging.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats_2: Dutch took two men out on a 'job' without asking Vic. Vic pretended not to care.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats_3: Payday was coming and the crew was restless. Vic asked us for shotgun shells to keep them loyal.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats_4a: With the shells we found, Vic kept the crew in line. Dutch sulked in a corner.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats_4b: No shells came, and Dutch challenged Vic openly. Half the crew listened to him.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats_4r: When the church raid came we sided with Vic. The job paid off, the crew loved him again, and Dutch went quiet.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats_5: To prove he was still the boss, Vic planned to crack the Coalfield bank vault. He asked us for a crowbar and a sledgehammer.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats_6a: With the tools we found, the vault opened. Nobody could touch Vic now, and he started turning the crew into traders.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats_6b: The vault stayed shut and Dutch took over the crew. Vic still called sometimes, but his voice was lower and the crew more dangerous.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter_1: A big black bear kept raiding Hank's trap lines, and he was tracking it.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter_2: Hank found a dead hiker in the woods and buried him. He said nothing more about it.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter_3: The bear hurt Hank's dog. He meant to finish it and asked us for rifle ammunition.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter_4a: With the rounds we sent, Hank got the bear. Smoked meat for weeks, and he almost smiled telling it.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter_4b: No rounds came, and the bear killed Hank's dog. He buried it by the creek and grew colder than ever.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter_4s: When the strange signal came we helped Hank. He scouted the tower himself; it was bandit bait, and he told only us.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter_5: Winter would come early in the woods. Hank asked us for a knife and twine to set new trap lines.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter_6a: With the knife and twine we sent, Hank was ready for winter. He called us 'neighbor' now, which is a lot, coming from him.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter_6b: His winter preparations failed. Hank started thinking about leaving the county for good.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_ray2a_1: Ray drove toward Louisville, sleeping in the pickup. The highway past Muldraugh was choked with wrecks and the dead.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_ray2a_2: A horde drifted onto the only road Ray could take, and he asked us to thin it out from our side.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_ray2a_3: We cleared the horde and the road opened. Ray reached the edge of Louisville, a city full of the dead.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_ray2a_3x: The road stayed blocked. Ray left the pickup and walked the last miles into Louisville.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_ray2a_4: Ray found the church shelter where Annie had stayed, surrounded by the dead. He needed shells and dressings to get in.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_ray2a_5a: With the shells we sent, Ray got inside and found Annie in the bell tower. They walked home to the farm together.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_ray2a_5d: Ray found Annie in the shelter's bell tower, and Dewey drove the Ark all the way to Louisville to bring them both home.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_ray2a_5x: The shelter had fallen weeks before. Annie's group had fled south, toward us, and someone had seen a girl in a yellow raincoat among the dead.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_ray2a_6: Annie had turned and was wandering near us. Ray could not do it himself and asked us to give her peace.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_ray2a_7r: We gave Annie peace and brought back her silver ring. Ray buried it under the apple tree, and he talks to her there in the evenings.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_ray2a_7x: Nobody gave Annie peace. Ray drove off alone to find his daughter himself.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_ray2b_1: A girl of about ten turned up alone and half starved at Ray's gate. She said her name was Lily, and nothing more.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_ray2b_2: Ray had nothing a child needs and asked us for food, medicine and something to make her smile.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_ray2b_3: With what we sent, Lily began to laugh. She helped in the garden and called him 'Mister Ray'.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_ray2b_3x: Nothing came, and Lily fell sick. Ray sat up with her every night.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_ray2b_4: A woman on the radio said she was Lily's mother and wanted to meet at the March Ridge church. Hank said the voice rode with raiders. We had to choose whom to help.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_ray2b_5a: The woman at the meeting really was Lily's mother. Lily went with her, and they visit the farm on Sundays.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_ray2b_5h: We trusted Hank. The 'mother' was raider bait, his warning shot scattered them, and Lily stayed with Ray.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_ray2b_5x: Only raiders came to the meeting. They took Lily, and Ray stopped tending the garden.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_casey2a_1: With her father back on his feet, Casey dreamed of a real relay so every survivor group in the county could hear each other.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_casey2a_2: The relay needed an amplifier, wire and parts, and Casey asked us.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_casey2a_3: With the parts we found, the relay worked. Three new groups checked in every night, and Casey read their news on the evening broadcast.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_casey2a_3x: No parts came and the relay kept burning out. Casey kept broadcasting with what she had.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_casey2a_4: Someone traced Casey's signal; a truck with no lights idled outside her shack for an hour. We had to choose who would protect her.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_casey2a_5a: The shack was safe, and Casey broadcasts 'Valley Station Free Radio' every night. People all over the county listen.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_casey2a_5x: Raiders smashed the relay and took the batteries. Casey and her father hid in the cellar, and she broadcasts only in whispers now.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_casey2b_1: A small voice answered Casey's broadcast: Toby, about nine, alone in an attic with his little sister.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_casey2b_2: The children were running out of food and water, and Casey asked us to send some.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_casey2b_3: The food we sent reached them. Every night Casey read the two of them stories until they fell asleep.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_casey2b_3x: No food reached them and Toby's voice grew weaker. Casey stayed on the frequency all night, talking to him.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_casey2b_4: The dead surrounded the house where the children were hiding, and Casey begged us to clear them.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_casey2b_5a: We cleared the dead and brought Toby and his sister out. They live in Casey's shack now, and Toby reads the morning weather.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_casey2b_5x: We never broke through, and Toby stopped answering. Casey still says goodnight to him on the air every night.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_doc2a_1: Marcus, June's best trainee, wore long sleeves in the heat and avoided her.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_doc2a_2: Marcus was hiding a bite, and only June did not know. We had to decide whom to turn to.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_doc2a_3a: We told June and brought her medicine. She tried everything, but Marcus died in the clinic holding her hand.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_doc2a_3p: We sent Marcus to Pike's church. He spent his last days in peace, with June beside him at the end.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_doc2a_3g: We left it to Whitaker, and his soldiers took Marcus away. June forgave no one.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_doc2a_3x: Nobody acted. Marcus turned in the clinic at night and bit another patient, and June stopped sleeping.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_doc2a_4: June wanted an isolation room so it would never happen again.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_doc2a_5a: With the materials we found, the clinic got its isolation room. Under one rule, nobody hides a bite, the helpers trusted June more than ever.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_doc2a_5m: The clinic got its isolation room, and Dewey turned the back of the Ark into a mobile clinic. Twice a week June rides out to distant farms.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_doc2a_5x: There was no isolation room. June checks everyone's arms at the door now, and lets the patients who stop coming go.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_doc2b_1: June stopped answering at night. Pike said she sat alone in the dark clinic.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_doc2b_2: Burned out, June said she needed something to get through the nights.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_doc2b_3: With what we sent, June slept a full night for the first time in a month. Pike came by and they talked until morning.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_doc2b_3x: June packed half the clinic into boxes, and kept unpacking them.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_doc2b_4: June said she would reopen only if she could do it properly, with real supplies.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_doc2b_5a: With the supplies we found, June reopened the clinic. It is smaller, but she tells everyone we talked her into coming back.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_doc2b_5p: June closed the clinic and became the nurse at Pike's church. It is quieter there, and she sleeps.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_pike2a_1: Word of the refuge spread. Forty people slept in the church, and more came every day.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_pike2a_2: The pantry could not feed forty, and Pike asked us for food.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_pike2a_3: The food we sent kept the pantry going. But crowds draw the dead, and more of them came to the fence each night.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_pike2a_3x: No food came, and hunger split the refugees. Some said the doors should close.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_pike2a_4: The church overflowed. Whitaker wanted to register everyone, Vic offered 'protection', and Pike wanted the doors open. It was up to us.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_pike2a_5a: With the planks and nails we sent, a second shelter went up. The church feeds sixty people, and the bell rings every Sunday.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_pike2a_5g: We backed Whitaker. His soldiers registered everyone and drafted the young men. The church is safe, and quiet.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_pike2a_5r: We chose Vic's 'protection'. Nobody steals from the church, but a share of every meal goes to Coalfield.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_pike2a_5x: No shelter was built and the doors closed. Pike turns people away every day, and it is breaking him.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_pike2b_1: Pike had not rung the bell since the night three died. He said he no longer knew what to pray for.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_pike2b_2: Ruth, the Sunday school teacher, one of the three, walked among the dead. Pike asked us to lay her to rest.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_pike2b_3: We laid Ruth to rest. Pike held his first funeral since the fall, and he sang.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_pike2b_3x: Ruth still walks out there. Some nights Pike sees her from the basement window.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_pike2b_4: Pike wanted to fix the bell rope and board up the tower so he could ring the bell again.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_pike2b_5a: With the rope and planks we sent, the bell rang again. People came out of hiding to listen, and Pike wept in front of them all.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_pike2b_5x: The bell never rang again. Pike took off his collar; he still looks after the people in the basement, but no longer calls himself a preacher.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey2a_1: Dewey promised to drive six people from the Echo Creek farms out of the county in the Ark.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey2a_2: Before the first run, the Ark needed spare tires and tools.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey2a_3: With the tires and tools we found loaded, Dewey test-drove to the county line and back, singing the whole way.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey2a_3x: No tires came. One blew on the test run and the Ark nearly rolled.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey2a_4: A horde gathered across the convoy road, more than even the Ark could push through.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey2a_5a: We cleared the horde and the convoy made it. Dewey drove six people past the county line and came back for more. They call the Ark 'the ferry' now.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey2a_5x: The horde was still there, and the Ark went into a ditch with everyone inside. Two did not get out. Dewey does not talk about the Ark.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey2b_1: Someone stole the Ark's engine block from Dewey's garage. Vic's boys had been seen nearby.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey2b_2: Vic said he 'found' the engine and would sell it back. It was up to us how Dewey got it back.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey2b_3a: We went into Coalfield with Dewey and took the engine back. Vic sulked, and Dewey could not stop grinning.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey2b_3r: We paid Vic. The engine came back, but Dewey still swears whenever it comes up.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey2b_3g: We left it to Whitaker, and his soldiers raided Coalfield and brought the engine back. Vic was furious with everyone.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey2b_3x: The engine never came back. Dewey sold the Ark's frame for parts and grew quiet.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey2b_4: With the engine back, Dewey meant to finish the Ark this time and asked us for parts, a battery and sheet metal.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey2b_5a: With the parts we found, the Ark finally ran. Two tries and one theft, Dewey says, make it a real Kentucky truck.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey2b_5x: The parts ran short again. The engine sits on a stand in the garage, and some nights Dewey polishes it.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard2a_1: A voice claiming to be battalion command broke weeks of silence on Whitaker's channel, with codes he half recognized.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard2a_2: Command ordered him to close the checkpoint and burn the refugee camp beside it as an infection risk. He had not answered yet.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard2a_3: Casey said the signal was fake and Pike begged him to refuse. We had to choose whose word to back.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard2a_4f: We helped Casey, who traced the 'command' signal to raiders using a stolen military radio. Whitaker was furious.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard2a_4p: We sided with Pike. Whitaker refused the order and sent the camp's people to the church; two soldiers called him a traitor and left.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard2a_4o: Whitaker sealed the checkpoint as ordered. The refugees burned their own shelters and left, and his squad would not meet his eyes.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard2a_4x: The checkpoint was never sealed, and command went silent again.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard2a_5: The noise at the checkpoint drew a horde toward the camp, and Whitaker called for support.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard2a_6a: We cleared the horde and the checkpoint held. Whitaker no longer waits for orders; he calls it 'our county'.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard2a_6f: We cleared the horde and the checkpoint held. With the raiders' radio smashed, Whitaker now trusts Casey's ears over any voice claiming rank.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard2a_6x: The horde broke the checkpoint. Whitaker led what was left north, and his frequency went dead.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard2b_1: Privates Cole and Mendez, Whitaker's deserters, had turned up working for Vic's crew.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard2b_2: Whitaker wanted them back for discipline, Vic would not give them up, and Ray was hiding the scared one at his farm. We had to choose.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard2b_3a: Cole came back on his own. Whitaker put him on latrine duty and said nothing more, and the squad noticed.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard2b_3r: We helped Ray. One deserter stayed hidden at his farm, and Whitaker stopped speaking to Ray.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard2b_3v: We backed Vic. Both deserters stayed with him, and now he knows the camp's watch schedule.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard2b_3x: The deserters vanished. Whitaker doubled the watch and sleeps in his boots.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard2b_4: Down to four soldiers, Whitaker asked us for sheet metal, nails and ammunition to fortify the camp before winter.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard2b_5a: With the materials we sent, the camp was fortified. The four of them hold it, and they trade with civilians at the gate.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard2b_5x: The camp could not be held. Whitaker walked north with the last of his squad.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats2a_1: The Iron Horse, a Louisville gang, said Coalfield was theirs now and Vic's trading post owed them half.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats2a_2: Vic said he needed guns to tell the Iron Horse no.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats2a_3: Showing the ammunition we found, Vic turned the Iron Horse away at the bridge. They promised to come back.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats2a_3x: No ammunition came, so Vic paid them tribute to buy time. The crew muttered that he had gone soft.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats2a_4: The Iron Horse drove the dead ahead of their attack, through our side of the county, and Vic asked us to break the herd.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats2a_5a: We broke the herd, and the Iron Horse broke on Vic's barricades. His trading post is the strongest thing in the south county.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats2a_5x: The herd was never broken. The Iron Horse reached the barricades, and Vic did not run.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats2b_1: Vic called on a different frequency. Dutch ran the crew like a warlord, and three of Vic's old boys wanted him back.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats2b_2: Vic asked us for weapons for the men still loyal to him.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats2b_3: With the weapons we found, Vic's boys were armed. He set the night.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats2b_3x: No weapons came, and one of the boys talked. Dutch knew something was coming.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats2b_4: Vic meant to take the crew back that night. Hank offered cover, and Whitaker wanted the whole crew arrested. It was up to us.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats2b_5a: Vic was the boss again. Dutch was gone, and the crew was smaller and quieter.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats2b_5g: We backed Whitaker. His soldiers raided Coalfield and Dutch was killed. Vic slipped away south and went off the air.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats2b_5x: Dutch found out. Vic went in anyway and did not come back. Only Dutch's threats come over the Coalfield frequency now.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter2a_1: In the pack of the hiker Hank had buried, he found a notebook. The man had been walking home to a wife and son.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter2a_2: The hiker's house was on our side of the county, thick with the dead. Hank asked us to clear it so he could see if the family was there.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter2a_3: We cleared the dead. The house was empty, with a note on the door: 'Gone to the March Ridge church.' Hank decided to carry the notebook there himself.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter2a_3x: Nobody got near the house. Hank read the notebook at night and talked about the man as if he had known him.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter2a_4: Hank set out to carry a dead man's notebook to his family and asked us for supplies for the trip.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter2a_5a: With the supplies we sent, Hank found the hiker's wife and gave her the notebook. She sends him preserves every month, and he pretends not to care.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter2a_5c: The family was safe at Pike's church. Hank gave them the notebook and stayed for supper, the first in years he had shared with anyone.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter2a_5x: Hank never found the family. The notebook sits on the shelf by his cabin door.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter2b_1: Hank packed to leave the county. One thing remained before he went: taking up his trap lines.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter2b_2: He needed a good knife and rope to take up the traps.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter2b_3: With the knife and rope we sent, the traps came up. Walking the lines one last time, Hank caught himself thinking about staying.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter2b_3x: Half the traps were left in the snow. Hank was angry about it, which meant he cared.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter2b_4: Hank said he would stay one more winter if the cabin had an axe for firewood and enough food stored.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter2b_5a: With the axe and food we sent, Hank stayed. Only one more winter, he says. Everyone knows better.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter2b_5x: Hank left. He left the cabin key under the stone by the door, for us.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_ray3_1a: Annie's working the fields beside me. First real harvest since it all fell apart, and I keep stopping just to watch her.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_ray3_1b: Lily's helping bring in the harvest, bossing the scarecrow around. First real harvest since the fall.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_ray3_1c: Bringing in the harvest alone. More corn and squash than one man could ever eat.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_ray3_2: Somebody's watching the farm from the treeline. Boot prints in the corn, and the dogs bark all night.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_ray3_3: Raiders are herding the dead toward my farm to run me off before the harvest is in. Can you help?
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_ray3_4: Fields are safe and the barn's full. I'd like to share it with Pike's church before winter.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_ray3_4x: While the dead kept me inside, they burned half the corn. I saved what I could.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_ray3_5: I need sacks and twine to haul the harvest over to the church.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_ray3_5x: Half the crop's ash. I'll need canned food to get through the winter.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_ray3_6a: My harvest fed Pike's church too. The preacher and I said grace together over the radio.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_ray3_6b: Kept the harvest, but couldn't haul it all. Some of it's rotting in the barn, and it eats at me.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_ray3_6c: Thanks to what you sent, the farm will make it through winter. Barely.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_ray3_6x: Barn's nearly empty going into winter. I'm rationing everything. Not going to complain.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_casey3_1a: The station's busy every night now. People I've never met know my voice.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_casey3_1b: I only broadcast at night now, quietly. Fewer people answer, but some still do.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_casey3_2: A man calling himself Private Ellis, an Army signals tech, asked to stay at the shack. He knows radios way better than me.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_casey3_3: I can't decide if I should trust Ellis. Sergeant Whitaker wants to check him out, and Hank wants to follow him.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_casey3_4a: Ellis was the real deal! He rebuilt my transmitter and taught me tricks I never knew.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_casey3_4g: Whitaker checked him out: a deserter, but harmless. Ellis joined the squad.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_casey3_4h: Hank followed Ellis to an Iron Horse camp. He was a spy. Hank ran him off. My hands are still shaking.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_casey3_4n: Ellis stayed a few nights, fixed a wire and moved on north. I never found out who he really was.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_casey3_4x: Ellis left in the night with half my batteries. I feel so stupid for letting him in.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_casey3_5: I want a backup transmitter before winter, so the county never goes quiet.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_casey3_5x: Without batteries I can only broadcast an hour a night.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_casey3_6a: I've got a backup transmitter! Whatever winter does, the county will hear me.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_casey3_6b: One transmitter, no backup. I keep my fingers crossed every night.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_casey3_6c: I'm back on the air every night. I don't let strangers in anymore.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_casey3_6x: Most nights I stay silent to save the batteries. I hate how quiet it is.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_doc3_1a: The clinic runs like a clinic again: a line in the morning, clean sheets, a schedule on the wall.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_doc3_1b: I'm the church's nurse now. I keep my kit in the vestry and see patients between prayers.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_doc3_1c: I still check every arm at the door. Fewer people come, but nobody has hidden a bite since.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_doc3_2: Medicine is running out county-wide. I want to grow herbs. The boy whose leg I set, older now, wants to be my apprentice.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_doc3_3: I need garden tools to start the herb beds.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_doc3_4: The herb beds are planted: chamomile, feverfew, willow cuttings. Pike's people came to help dig.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_doc3_4x: No tools came. The boy and I are drying wild herbs from the riverbank instead.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_doc3_5: A pack of the dead is drifting through the fields toward the clinic. My apprentice wants to fight. I won't let him.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_doc3_6a: The herb garden is growing and my apprentice learns fast. Willow bark for pain, chamomile for sleep. Not much, but ours.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_doc3_6b: No garden, but my apprentice knows which riverbank weeds bring a fever down. I'm proud of him.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_doc3_6x: The dead trampled everything, and my apprentice got hurt trying to stop them. He'll heal. I'm not sure I will.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_pike3_1a: The church is full of life. Children run between the pews and someone is always cooking.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_pike3_1b: Someone else keeps order at the church now. I still lead the prayers, and people still come to me.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_pike3_1c: The church is quieter than it was. I look after the few who stayed.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_pike3_2: Two refugees, Daniel and Rosa, asked me to marry them. It would be the county's first wedding since the fall.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_pike3_3: I'd like a real wedding feast, with candles and something to toast with.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_pike3_4: Everyone is invited. Ray promised vegetables, and Casey will broadcast the vows.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_pike3_4x: There will be no feast, only vows. Daniel and Rosa say that is enough.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_pike3_5: The dead are gathering on the road to the church the day before the wedding.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_pike3_6a: Daniel and Rosa were married with candles and a feast. Half the county listened, and I wept again.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_pike3_6b: A simple wedding: vows, a borrowed ring, a hymn. Everyone came, and nobody missed the feast.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_pike3_6x: We held the wedding in the basement while the dead beat on the doors. A guest was bitten on the way in.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_dewey3_1a: The Ark runs and everybody wants a ride somewhere. It drinks fuel like you wouldn't believe.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_dewey3_1b: No Ark, but the garage is busy. Everybody in the county brings me something broken.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_dewey3_2: Gas is running out across the county. Every pump I know is bone dry.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_dewey3_3: Found a gas station with a full underground tank. Thing is, it's crawling with the dead.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_dewey3_4: Station's clear and the tank's full. Now I just need a pump and hoses to get it out.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_dewey3_4x: Couldn't get to the tank. I'm siphoning wrecks one can at a time.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_dewey3_5: I need hoses and tools to draw the fuel out of that tank.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_dewey3_5x: Siphoning takes hoses, and I keep wrecking mine.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_dewey3_6a: Fuel for the whole winter. Half the county runs on gas I pumped, and I like that more than I let on.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_dewey3_6b: The tank's right there, but I'm bucketing it out. It'll do for now.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_dewey3_6c: Can by can, I scraped together enough for winter. My hands smell like gas all the time.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_dewey3_6x: No fuel. The garage is cold, and the engines in it are just metal now.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_guard3_1a: The checkpoint holds. Civilians pass every day, and more of them stop to talk to the soldiers.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_guard3_1b: The camp holds with four of us. Civilians trade at the gate, and some of them linger.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_guard3_2: Civilians asked me to train them. I refused twice. Then a farm kid died because nobody taught him to hold a rifle.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_guard3_3: I am training volunteers. I need practice ammunition.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_guard3_4: The volunteers can shoot now. Live drill next, against real dead, and I will watch every one of them.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_guard3_4x: Training without ammunition is just shouting. Some quit. A few stayed.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_guard3_5: Running a live drill against a real group of the dead. Requesting the players' support.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_guard3_6a: The county has a militia: twelve volunteers who can hold a line. I will not say I am proud of them.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_guard3_6b: A small militia: five volunteers, green but brave. It is a start.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_guard3_6x: A volunteer died in the drill. I disbanded them. I do it all myself again.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_rats3_1a: My trading post is the strongest thing in the south county. People come from farther every week.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_rats3_1b: The crew's smaller and quieter since Dutch. I'm trying something new: being trusted.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_rats3_2: I'm holding a market day in Coalfield, first since the fall. Anyone can come. No robbing. Vic's word.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_rats3_3: The stalls need goods. Food, tools, bandages.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_rats3_4: Stalls are full. Painted the sign myself. It's crooked.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_rats3_4x: The stalls are thin. I'll sell what I've got and talk big about the rest.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_rats3_5: A horde's drifting toward Coalfield on market day.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_rats3_6a: Market day was a hit. Made it monthly. People shake my hand now. Don't know what to do with that.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_rats3_6b: Small market, but nobody got robbed and everybody went home alive. I call that a win.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_rats3_6x: The dead broke up the market and a trader died. Nobody came back the next month.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_hunter3_1a: Autumn in the woods. Lines at dawn, the hiker's notebook by the fire.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_hunter3_1b: I stayed, and autumn came. Cabin's warm. I stayed for the deer. Let's leave it at that.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_hunter3_2: Something's springing my traps and taking the catch. Not an animal. Small boot prints. Careful ones.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_hunter3_3: Going to track it for days. Need supplies for it.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_hunter3_4: Found the thief. A starving young deserter, one of Whitaker's. Have to decide what to do with him.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_hunter3_4x: Never found the thief. The stealing just stopped. I still check for prints every morning.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_hunter3_6a: The kid lives at the cabin now, learning traps. Talks too much. I let him.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_hunter3_6g: Whitaker took the kid back. Right by the book. I hate the book.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_hunter3_6r: The kid works Ray's farm now. I visit Sundays. Say it's for the pie.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_hunter3_6n: Left food at the lean-to and walked off. He's gone now. Hope he made it.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_hunter3_6x: The kid ran off into the cold before anyone could help. Lean-to was empty the next week.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_martha1_1: I took over Ray's farm and his radio. Found his notebook of frequencies too. Keep it by the set.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_nora1_1: I came down from Brandenburg to keep Casey's frequency alive. Her logbook is full of names. I'm learning them one by one.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_sam1_1: I'm running June's clinic now, with her notes and her kit. I'm seventeen. Honestly, I'm terrified.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_esther1_1: There's no preacher at the church now. I keep the kitchen going and the doors open, and I answer the radio.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_lenny1_1: I'm running Dewey's garage now. I know half of what she knew. I talk to her tools when nobody's around.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_kowalski1_1: I am in command of what is left of the squad. Nobody trained me for this. Everyone is watching me. ...Out.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_red1_1: I'm holding the Coalfield crew together since the raid. Fewer fights, more deals.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_dutch1_1: Coalfield's mine now. Vic's gone. Everyone on this frequency is going to learn some respect.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Story_caleb1_1: I came looking for Hank and found his cabin empty. I stayed. My father would've wanted someone to keep the lines.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_ray3_1a: Annie worked the fields beside Ray. The first real harvest since the fall was coming in.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_ray3_1b: Lily helped Ray bring in the harvest, the first real one since the fall.

IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_ray3_5: Ray asked for sacks and twine to haul the harvest to the church.

IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_ray3_6c: With the cans we sent, Ray's farm would just about make it through winter.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_ray3_6x: No cans came. Ray went into winter with a nearly empty barn.

IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_casey3_6a: With the parts we found, Casey built a backup transmitter. Whatever winter brings, the county will hear her.

IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_casey3_6c: With the batteries we sent, Casey is back on the air every night. She lets no strangers in now.

IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey3_1a: The Ark ran, and drank fuel like nothing else.

IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_dewey3_2: Gasoline was running out across the county.

IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard3_6a: The drill went well with us there. The county had a militia.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard3_6b: The drill went well. A small militia, but a start.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_guard3_6x: A volunteer died in the drill, and Whitaker disbanded them.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats3_1a: Vic's trading post was the strongest thing in the south county.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats3_1b: Since Dutch, Vic's crew had grown smaller and quieter.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats3_2: Vic decided to hold Coalfield's first market day. Anyone could come; no robbing.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats3_3: Vic asked for goods to fill the stalls.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats3_4: With the goods we sent, the stalls were full.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats3_4x: No goods came, and the stalls were thin.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats3_5: On market day a horde drifted toward Coalfield.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats3_6a: We cleared the horde. Market day was a hit and became monthly.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats3_6b: We cleared the horde. A small market, but everyone got home safe.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_rats3_6x: The horde broke up the market, and a trader died.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter3_1a: Autumn came to the woods. Hank checked his lines every dawn.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter3_1b: Autumn came for Hank, who had stayed.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter3_2: Something sprang Hank's traps and stole the catch, leaving small boot prints.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter3_3: Hank asked for supplies to track the thief for days.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter3_4: With the supplies we sent, Hank found the thief: a starving young deserter. We had to decide what to do with him.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter3_4x: The thief was never found, and the stealing stopped on its own.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter3_6a: The boy lives at Hank's cabin now, learning traps.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter3_6g: Whitaker took the boy back. Hank hated the book that said so.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter3_6r: The boy became Ray's farm hand, and Hank visits on Sundays.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter3_6n: Hank left food and walked away. The boy was gone.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_hunter3_6x: The boy ran off into the cold before anyone could help.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_martha1_1: Ray's neighbor Martha Cole took over his farm and his radio.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_nora1_1: Nora Bell, a radio operator from Brandenburg, took over Casey's frequency.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_sam1_1: Sam, June's seventeen-year-old apprentice, took over the clinic.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_esther1_1: Esther Gray, who ran the church kitchen, began answering the radio.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_lenny1_1: Lenny Austin, Dewey's apprentice, took over the garage.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_kowalski1_1: Corporal Kowalski took command of what was left of the squad.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_red1_1: Red, who had stayed with the crew, held Coalfield together.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Tale_caleb1_1: Earl's son, Caleb Tate, took over Hank's cabin.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Crisis_ellis: A man calling himself Private Ellis has been staying at Casey's shack. Casey wants to trust him, Whitaker wants to check him, and Hank wants to follow him.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Crisis_ellis_casey: Asks for food and blankets to keep her guest properly.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Crisis_ellis_guard: Will pick Ellis up and check his story if given 5.56 ammunition.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Crisis_ellis_hunter: Will follow Ellis to see where he really goes if given rifle ammunition.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Crisis_thief: The thief raiding Hank's traps is a starving young deserter from Whitaker's squad. Hank could take him in, Whitaker wants him back, and Ray could use a farm hand.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Crisis_thief_hunter: Asks for food and blankets so he can take the boy in.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Crisis_thief_guard: Will send the squad to collect their deserter if given 5.56 ammunition.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Crisis_thief_ray: Asks for canned food to feed the boy as a farm hand.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Profile_doc_family_appr: Apprentice - the boy whose leg she set
IGUI_StoryEngine_Profile_guard_family_mi: The squad and a twelve-strong civilian militia
IGUI_StoryEngine_Profile_hunter_family_a: A young deserter living at the cabin, learning traps
IGUI_StoryEngine_Profile_martha_home: Ray Mercer's farmhouse outside West Point
IGUI_StoryEngine_Profile_martha_bio: The widow from the farm next to Ray's, who promised to watch his farm. Blunt, generous, and allergic to sentiment.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Profile_nora_bio: A radio operator from Brandenburg who used to listen to Casey. Calm, wry, organized. Learning the county from Casey's logbook.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Profile_sam_family: Lost his family, grew up at the clinic
IGUI_StoryEngine_Profile_sam_bio: The boy whose broken leg June set, now her seventeen-year-old apprentice, running the clinic with her notes. Earnest, scared, learning fast.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Profile_esther_family: The church folk are her family
IGUI_StoryEngine_Profile_esther_job: Ran the church kitchen and storeroom
IGUI_StoryEngine_Profile_esther_bio: The woman who ran the church kitchen and storeroom. She doesn't preach; she keeps the place running. Practical, warm, no patience for nonsense.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Profile_lenny_bio: A young man Dewey was teaching. Eager, clumsy, and he worshipped Dewey.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Profile_kowalski_bio: The last corporal of Whitaker's squad, suddenly in command. Tries to sound like Whitaker and fails.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Profile_red_bio: A sharp-tongued woman who stayed with the crew after the raid. Tired of fighting; wants more deals and fewer fights.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Profile_dutch_bio: Vic's former second, now running the Coalfield crew like a warlord. Menacing, greedy, enjoys threats.
IGUI_StoryEngine_Profile_caleb_family: His father Earl was Hank's hunting partner
IGUI_StoryEngine_Profile_caleb_home: The cabin in the Ekron woods
IGUI_StoryEngine_Profile_caleb_bio: Son of Hank's late hunting partner Earl. Came looking for Hank and took over the empty cabin. Quiet like Hank, gentler.
